newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macmin reports PNG copper find.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macmin reports PNG copper find.

text.p: Macmin NL said on Monday exploration has revealed a promising copper system at its 45 percent-owned Simuku mine prospect in Papua New Guinea.
The Queensland-based explorer said two drill holes at Simuku, located near the port of Kimbe on the island of New Britain, had interesected porphyry copper mineralisation.
One hole intersected mineralisation throughout its entire length, terminating in potentially economic copper grades, the company said.
A 47-metre section between 16 metres and 63 metres averaged 0.58 percent copper, 80 parts per million (ppm) molybdenum and 0.11 grammes of gold a tonne, Macmin said.
The entire hole averaged 0.5 percent copper, 65 ppm molybdenum and 0.11 g/t gold, it added.
A second hole averaged 0.23 percent copper, 0.12 g/t gold and 15 ppm molybdenum, Macmin said.
The mineralisation is open in all directions and evidence so far suggest a large system, although a great deal more drilling will be required to confirm the test work, the company said.
Further test drilling is scheduled to start next week, Bob McNeil, Macmin's managing director, told Reuters.
Macmin's partner, New Guinea Gold Corp, is earning a 55 percent interest in Simuku through exploration funding.
